reasoning.title: Run the dated Bestsellers report

reasoning.content: Do not treat the first product row—or a brand inferred from its name—as the top brand. Export the visible report using “Export to:” when necessary, map products to their brand attribute, aggregate the sales measure by brand, and answer only from that grounded comparison.

reasoning.title: Use the Period control as grouping, not range
reasoning.description: When running Reports → Products → Bestsellers for a date-bounded period such as a quarter; not when a yearly breakdown is explicitly requested.
reasoning.content: Enter the From and To dates, then choose “Month” or retain a suitable finer grouping before running the report. Selecting “Year” does not combine an arbitrary partial-year range into a trustworthy quarter total and can obscure the needed comparison.

reasoning.title: Do not mistake the leading product for the leading brand
reasoning.description: When the requested ranking is by brand but the available “Bestsellers” report lists products; not when the task asks directly for the top product.
reasoning.content: Generate the filtered report, inspect the visible result rows, map products to their brands, and aggregate the sales measure across all products for each brand. Never answer from a product name, dashboard widget, or assumed brand unless the report data visibly supports the aggregation.

reasoning.title: Complete type-and-quantity join

reasoning.content: Record every result row’s product name and quantity, then open Catalog > Products and use the grid’s Name and Type columns to classify every recorded product. Sum quantities by Type and compare those totals; never infer the winner from a subset of products or from product counts.

reasoning.title: Clear persistent catalog filters
reasoning.description: Use when Catalog > Products opens with an “Active filters” banner or a prefilled “Search by keyword” box; not needed when the grid is visibly unfiltered and contains every product being checked.
reasoning.content: Catalog grid filters persist across navigation and can silently expose only matching products. Click “Clear all,” then search each report product individually—or apply a complete multi-product filter—and verify that every report row has a recorded Type before answering.

reasoning.title: Use the Products Bestsellers report
reasoning.description: When answering product-sales rankings for a specified period; not when the unfiltered Dashboard Bestsellers widget already matches the requested scope.
reasoning.content: Open “REPORTS,” choose “Bestsellers” under the product reports, set “Period,” complete the required “From” and “To” fields, and click “Show Report.” The Dashboard widget is a look-alike summary and should not be used for a historical period unless its scope is visibly confirmed.

reasoning.title: Require visible result rows
reasoning.description: After clicking “Show Report,” when product names or rankings must be returned; not while only the filter form or normalized date values are visible.
reasoning.content: Wait for the report to finish loading, then scroll or inspect beyond the filter panel until the results table and its ranked product rows are visibly observed. Return only the requested leading rows and never infer names from prior knowledge, the URL, or the unchanged filter form.

reasoning.title: Verify the rendered Bestsellers results
reasoning.description: Use for historical best-selling-product questions after opening Reports > Products > Bestsellers and applying the Period, From, and To filters; do not use the dashboard bestseller widget as a substitute.
reasoning.content: After clicking “Show Report,” scroll past the Filter and Export controls until the results grid is visible, then confirm its column headings and inspect every page or export the complete report. Identify the row with the greatest quantity sold from actual result data before drawing any conclusion.

reasoning.title: Confirm type in the product record
reasoning.description: Use when a report identifies a product but does not explicitly display its Magento product type; skip only if the result itself contains a verified Product Type field.
reasoning.content: Copy the winning product’s exact name or SKU, go to Catalog > Products, and search for that exact identifier. Open the matching product record and read its displayed product type; never infer type from the name, SKU, or prior knowledge.

reasoning.title: Use the historical Bestsellers report
reasoning.description: Use this for bestseller questions scoped to a past date range; do not use the Dashboard Bestsellers widget, which is not reliably scoped to the requested period.
reasoning.content: Open “REPORTS,” then choose “Bestsellers” under “Products.” Set “Period” to the requested grouping, fill both “From” and “To,” and run the report with “Show Report.”

reasoning.title: Ground the ranking in generated results
reasoning.description: Apply when identifying the leading product or product type after filtering; do not answer from memory, the dashboard widget, or filters alone.
reasoning.content: Wait for the filtered results table, verify the displayed date scope, and read the highest-ranked row by the report’s sales quantity. If the report shows a product name rather than its type, open or look up that product’s catalog details before reporting the type.

reasoning.title: Verify the rendered result set
reasoning.description: Apply after “Show Report” reloads the page, especially when the current observation displays only filters and not the report table.

Scroll below the filters and inspect pagination or use the “Export to:” control to obtain the complete result set, then rank products using the displayed sales metric and preserve the report’s ordering for ties.

reasoning.title: Verify the result grid before answering
reasoning.description: Applies after “Show Report” reloads the report; do not answer if only the filter panel is visible or no result rows have been inspected.
reasoning.content: Navigate below the Filter and Export controls until the report grid is visible, then read the leading rows and their sales-quantity values in displayed rank order. Check pagination or export the report if needed to verify the requested count; if no rows are observable, report that the ranking cannot be confirmed rather than supplying names from memory or another widget.

reasoning.title: Use the Orders grid for status-qualified counts

Open Sales > Orders, expand “Filters,” choose the requested value in “Status,” apply the filter, and export the filtered order rows for aggregation.

reasoning.title: Aggregate and verify every tied customer

Before answering, verify the active filter and cite inspected rows or exported data; never infer a name from an uninspected or partially rendered report.

reasoning.title: Export and aggregate the complete report

reasoning.title: Retrieve the full filtered order set

reasoning.title: Aggregate before ranking

reasoning.title: Verify the generated results grid

reasoning.title: Verify the generated report table

reasoning.title: Reveal and set the status filter

reasoning.title: Verify the regenerated results table

reasoning.title: Configure the Orders report status filter

reasoning.title: Configure the Orders report by labels

reasoning.content: Navigate through “Reports” to the Sales “Orders” report, set the “Period,” “From,” and “To” fields, then change “Order Status” from “Any” to “Specified” and select the visible status label required by the task. reasoning.title: Verify the generated result table

reasoning.title: Open the complete reviews grid

reasoning.title: Open the customer review grid
